summary.text: A right-handed 25-year-old male fire alarm repair technician presented with inability to extend his right index finger since 3 months after a trivial, blunt trauma to the dorsum of his distal forearm. He had sustained a distal radius fracture in the same limb 2.5 years ago due to an accidental fall, fixed with an intramedullary titanium elastic nail system (TENS), after which he regained full wrist and finger motion.

Examination showed complete loss of active extension of the right index finger at the MCP joint, with extension of the other fingers and the thumb preserved. Ultrasonography showed complete discontinuity of both EDC and EIP tendons of the index finger with a 6-cm gap, and radiographs showed the TENS nail in the radius with its dorsal tip abutting the extensor compartment. The authors state the cause was chronic attrition against newly formed bone around the retained nail.

Under regional anesthesia a Z incision was made on the dorsal wrist and distal forearm, and the extensor retinaculum was partially opened. Both tendons were ruptured with frayed cut ends about 6 cm apart and the EPL intact. New bone at the nail entry point was removed by burring, the nail could not be removed, its protruding end was cut short and the remainder left in place. The EDC was reconstructed with a palmaris longus graft; the very thin EIP was not reconstructed.

A postoperative radiograph showed the shortened nail no longer impinging the extensor compartment. The hand was immobilized in a volar splint for 3 weeks, and early active supervised physiotherapy was started thereafter. At 6 weeks follow-up the patient could make a fist and regained useful range of index finger extension, and the authors describe excellent functional recovery.
